text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a ‘midstream-pause’ handshake for the edge proxy so backends can temporarily pause streaming without forcing client reconnects. thinking this helps model queueing + rate-limit scenarios.
rohan: curious, how is this different from current soft-fallback / resume tokens?
kai: +1 on investigating. my concern: this changes connection semantics and will affect tracing and SLOs.
maria: good q. current resume is for hard cutoffs (connection dropped, then resumed). pause is explicit: proxy signals client "we're pausing, keepalive expected" and backend returns a pause token.
sasha: sketch of header idea:
```
X-Edge-Pause: pause_token=abc123; ttl=15s; reason=backend-queue
X-Edge-Pause-Mode: keepalive|poll
```
kai: interesting. what does keepalive vs poll do?
maria: keepalive: server keeps TCP open and streams periodic pings. poll: client switches to periodic status-checks (HTTP) until resume. poll is cheaper on long stalls but loses streaming immediacy.
rohan: implications: 1) need to surface metrics (edge.pause.count, edge.pause.duration) 2) retry budget interaction — paused requests shouldn't consume retry credits but also shouldn't be requeued.
sasha: we also need idempotency constraints: if a pause crosses a request boundary where downstream may have partially applied side effects, rollbacks are hard. maybe restrict pause to read-only/generative paths.
taylor: UX question: how does SDK surface this? do we expose an event hook like onPause(token, ttl)?
maria: yes — SDK should emit onPause and onResume; also allow user opt-out to always fallback to immediate reconnect.
deploy-bot: diff attached (partial):
```
diff --git a/proxy/edge/handshake.go b/proxy/edge/handshake.go
+ // add Pause token negotiation
+ func negotiatePause(...) { /* ... */ }
```
rohan: tradeoffs: state we add to proxy (pause table), GC for stale tokens, and attacker surface — someone could hold connections open. need per-tenant pause quota and short TTLs.
kai: also consider observability: make pause a first-class trace span and annotate logs: `pause_token=%s pause_ttl=%ds` so we can correlate.
sasha: fallback: if client doesn't support pause, proxy must degrade to existing behavior. that implies header negotiation in initial handshake: `X-Edge-Features: pause-v1`
maria: agreed. compatibility path: if client lacks pause support, we either 1) stream an abbreviated terminal trailer that asks client to reconnect or 2) switch to poll mode automatically. prefer automatic poll for mobile clients.
taylor: perf concern: poll mode will increase request churn on busy tenants. we should provide recommended defaults per tenant: short TTL + poll interval backoff.
rohan: ops: add alert when pause durations spike above baseline (pause.duration > p50*4). also add dashboard: paused flows by model & route.
kai: security: pause tokens should be HMAC'd by control plane and bound to tenant+route+expiry. no unbounded tokens.
sasha: can we reuse existing resume token format? keeps impl small. but resume tokens embed KV cache offsets currently. might be separate types.
maria: probably separate but share underlying signing. implementation plan: (1) handshakes + headers + SDK hooks (2) pause table and GC + quotas (3) metrics & traces + dashboards (4) opt-out flag per route.
rohan: +1. propose we run a 2-week experiment behind a feature flag on a single model route. can we add synthetic load tests?
taylor: I'll add a small perf suite that simulates model stalls and measures 99p latency and connection retention.
maria: thanks. next steps: I'll write a follow-up RFC with header proto, token format, and abort rules. tagging @kai @sasha for security/observability review. :eyes:
rohan: :thumbsup:
